title: The day we tested soil at Antelope Wells
summary: Three test blocks, one cracked. That crack changed the mix — and the budget conversation.
body:
We rammed three test blocks from the building site: 6%, 8% and 10% cement. The 6% block cracked on day three, exactly as the engineer suspected. 8% held.

That test cost $900 in this story and saved a wall. It is why phase 01 exists and why I don't quote earth walls from a photograph of dirt.

title: West light, 6:42 pm, Chinati View
summary: Stood on the cabin site at sunset to place the one big window. It will not face the view you expect.
body:
The postcard view is west — straight into the setting sun. We put the big glass north-east to the mountains and gave the west a solid earth wall and a slot window at standing eye height.

The clients stood there with me at 6:42 pm. That ten minutes did more than three renderings.

title: What the Valentine roof actually needed
summary: Opening the schoolhouse roof found sistered trusses everywhere. Contingency rules changed after this.
body: Every truss needed a sister. It added five weeks in this story and taught me to write 15% contingency into any reuse phase 01 — and to say it out loud before design, not during construction.

title: Rain on a fresh lift
summary: A summer storm hit a rammed lift before it cured. We removed it the next morning.
body: Weather in the desert is not a metaphor. The lift slumped, we cut it out, and the wall schedule now carries two weather days per lift — written into the builder's price, not hoped away.
